title: RF exposure and safety
blurb: Why radio waves heat rather than ionize, what sets your exposure, and who has to make sure your station complies.

T0C01.why: Radio waves are **non-ionizing** radiation: they don't have enough energy to strip electrons from atoms.
T0C01.trap: Gamma, alpha and ionizing radiation are the radioactive kind.

T0C02.why: The body absorbs RF best around VHF, so the exposure limit is **lowest near 50 MHz**.
T0C02.trap: Higher frequency doesn't mean lower limit: the curve dips, then rises toward microwaves.

T0C03.why: Limits apply to **average** exposure. Transmitting half the time halves the average, so the allowed level **doubles**.
T0C03.trap: Lower duty cycle loosens, never tightens, the allowance.

T0C04.why: Frequency, power, distance and antenna pattern **all** affect exposure.

T0C05.why: The body **absorbs more RF energy at some frequencies** than at others, so the limits differ by frequency.
T0C05.trap: Lower frequencies don't carry more energy, and RF does penetrate the body.

T0C06.why: **Calculation** (OET Bulletin 65), **computer modeling** and **measurement** with calibrated equipment are all acceptable.

T0C07.why: Touching an antenna while transmitting can give an **RF burn** to the skin.
T0C07.trap: RF isn't ionizing, and burns are the hazard, not electrocution.

T0C08.why: Moving the **antennas** away from people reduces exposure. Moving only the transmitter doesn't change the field at the antenna.
T0C08.trap: More duty cycle means more average exposure.

T0C09.why: Re-evaluate your station **whenever any transmitter or antenna part changes**, since the exposure may change.
T0C09.trap: Telling the FCC, low SWR or approved gear doesn't show your station still complies.

T0C10.why: Exposure limits are based on **average** exposure, and duty cycle sets how much of the time you transmit.
T0C10.trap: It doesn't change peak levels, feed line loss or amplifier heating.

T0C11.why: Duty cycle is the **percentage of time** the transmitter is transmitting during the averaging time.
T0C11.trap: Don't flip it: not transmitting is the opposite.

T0C12.why: RF doesn't have enough energy to cause **chemical changes or DNA damage**, unlike ionizing radiation. It's still not "perfectly safe".

T0C13.why: The **station licensee** must make sure no one is exposed above the FCC limits.
T0C13.trap: The FCC sets the limits; responsibility rests with the licensee.
